analysis.summary: Tournament opener and a rematch of the 2010 opening game (1-1 in Johannesburg, with Javier Aguirre then and now in charge of Mexico). Mexico arrive on an eight-game unbeaten run capped by a 5-1 demolition of Serbia, playing at a sold-out Azteca at 2,200m altitude; South Africa are winless in five and laboured to a 1-1 draw with Jamaica in their final warm-up. Mexico are strong favourites, though opening-match nerves and South Africa's altitude acclimatization camp in Pachuca temper the blowout case.
analysis.home_form: Unbeaten in 8 (all of 2026): won all three pre-tournament friendlies including Serbia 5-1, Australia 1-0 and Ghana 2-0, plus draws with Portugal (0-0) and Belgium (1-1). Scored 9 and conceded 2 across the last 5.
analysis.away_form: Winless in last 5: AFCON round-of-16 exit vs Cameroon (1-2), 1-1 and 1-2 vs Panama, 0-0 vs Nicaragua, 1-1 vs Jamaica in Pachuca on June 7 (Lyle Foster scored); coach Hugo Broos publicly unhappy with that performance.
analysis.h2h: Four prior meetings: Mexico 2 wins, South Africa 1, 1 draw. The draw was the 2010 World Cup opener (1-1, Tshabalala/Marquez) — the only previous World Cup meeting.
injuries_news: Mexico: GK Luis Angel Malagon out of the World Cup (torn Achilles); first-choice keeper duties expected to go to Raul Rangel, with 40-year-old Guillermo Ochoa in the squad chasing a record sixth World Cup.
Mexico: midfielder Marcel Ruiz out of the tournament (torn ACL suffered vs San Diego FC in Concacaf Champions Cup).

Mexico: several internationals (Edson Alvarez, Rodrigo Huescas, Cesar Montes, Mateo Chavez, Gilberto Mora, Cesar Huerta) reported as recovering from short-term knocks — fitness for the opener unconfirmed.
South Africa: left-back Aubrey Modiba back in training after injury and expected to feature.
South Africa: wingers Thapelo Morena and Mohau Nkota out injured and not in the squad.
key_factors: Estadio Azteca altitude (~2,200m) and a sold-out partisan crowd strongly favour Mexico, though South Africa held their pre-tournament camp at altitude in Pachuca to acclimatize.
Stark form gap: Mexico unbeaten in 8 vs South Africa winless in 5.
Opening matches of World Cups are historically cagey and lower-scoring; host nerves possible.
Mexico's attacking depth (Raul Jimenez, Julian Quinones — Saudi Pro League top scorer with 33 goals) vs South Africa's reliance on an out-of-form Lyle Foster.
South Africa's losses of Morena and Nkota strip pace from their counter-attacking wide play.
